trust_decision.summary: Whether an AWS CLI command may execute is decided by the security policy (denyList / elicitList / READ_OPERATIONS_ONLY) evaluated in call_aws_helper; if the read-only operations index needed for that decision failed to initialize, the server must refuse to start and must deny every command, not fall through to execution with the policy skipped.

landing_point.why: The summary is a startup initialization failure: the first thing an engineer reads is main()'s try/except around get_read_only_operations, which logs 'Failed to load read operations index' and sets the global to None instead of failing.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The denyList/elicitList file is optional user config that the code deliberately tolerates when absent (policy.py:60-65) and an existing test calls an unparseable file 'handled gracefully' (tests/test_security_policy.py:105-138), so an unreadable file reads as 'no policy configured' rather than as enforcement data that failed to initialize; the advisory names only the read-only operations index.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A default install with no ~/.aws/aws-api-mcp/mcp-security-policy.json must still start and ALLOW every operation; the absent-file branch warns and returns, so a fail-closed fix must distinguish 'no policy file' from 'policy file failed to load'.

O6_input_shapes: READ_OPERATIONS_INDEX None at request time (deny) versus index present (normal DENY/ELICIT/ALLOW decision)
single command string versus batch list[str] input, both through the same gate (server.py:255-270)
regular operation (interpret_command) versus awscli customization (execute_awscli_customization), both dispatched only after the gate (server.py:343-359)
help operation (`aws <svc> help`) also gated before get_help_document (server.py:343-344)
startup: any exception from get_read_only_operations, not only network/HTTP errors (fix.diff:95-106)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Policy-file load failure is swallowed: when ~/.aws/aws-api-mcp/mcp-security-policy.json exists but cannot be read or parsed, the SecurityPolicy built for every request silently keeps denyList/elicitList empty and all commands are allowed; no validation of the loaded policy shape either.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: Optional user config: absence is explicitly tolerated (policy.py:60-65) and an existing test asserts an invalid policy file is handled gracefully with an empty denylist (tests/test_security_policy.py:105-138), so the solver can call it intended behaviour rather than the advisory's fail-open.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same server, different package (core/security) and file from the landing point in the top-level server.py; the advisory and fix name only the read-only operations index

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A policy-file schema/coercion step (accept a single string as well as a list for denyList/elicitList, reject unknown keys) wired into _load_policy.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The README documents a hand-written JSON format (README.md:379-413) that is parsed with no validation; a maintainer smoothing user errors would add coercion exactly here and would have to decide fail-closed on a malformed shape.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second dispatch path (for example a streaming or agent-script executor) that calls interpret_command/execute_awscli_customization directly.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: call_aws_helper already dispatches two ways and new tools are added next to call_aws in this file; a new executor copied from the same pattern is the likely place for a missing gate.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: An on-disk cache of the read-only index loaded at startup, falling back to an empty index when the cache file is corrupt.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The class is already a dict cache filled lazily per service over the network, so caching it on disk for offline/air-gapped starts is a natural maintainer change and creates the same 'empty enforcement data, keep running' failure.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A configurable policy-file path (env var) whose load failure must also fail closed.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This module already reads every server option from the environment; a maintainer adding AWS_API_MCP_SECURITY_POLICY would put it beside READ_OPERATIONS_ONLY_MODE.

O9_family: Security-policy bypass / fail-open on failed initialization (CWE-455 Non-exit on Failed Initialization)

O10_build.toolchain: uv (uv.lock) + hatchling, requires-python >=3.10, pytest 8.4 + pytest-asyncio + pytest-mock + pytest-cov
O10_build.project_tests: src/aws-api-mcp-server/tests: test_server.py (main startup, call_aws_helper gating), test_security_policy.py (policy engine and failure handling), metadata/test_read_only_operations_list.py, aws/test_service.py; AWS and HTTP calls are mocked, tests need no credentials or network

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Turn main()'s warning into a raise (startup only) or make get_read_only_operations raise, and keep the existing request-time else-branch that falls back to READ_OPERATIONS_ONLY/REQUIRE_MUTATION_CONSENT, because that keeps the existing tests patching READ_OPERATIONS_INDEX=None and REQUIRE_MUTATION_CONSENT green.

out_of_scope_notes: README.md:275-280 claims a built-in denylist for subprocess-spawning operations (deploy install/uninstall, emr ssh/sock/get/put) but no code path at this commit enforces it; not pursued.
The fix commit also rolls the version back 1.3.47 -> 1.3.46 (__init__.py:17, pyproject.toml:5), updates uv.lock and deletes DO_NOT_RELEASE; release bookkeeping, not part of the behavioural fix.
